title: p2peace Citizenship v1 (taxes.gov.example)
description: Proves receipt of a DKIM-signed institutional notice from an allowlisted government domain, addressed to an inbox the prover controls. Reveals nothing about the recipient: the to-address is captured privately, canonicalized, and hashed with a registration salt into a per-address nullifier. One blueprint instance is compiled per allowlisted government domain; this file is the instance for the example domain taxes.gov.example. The proof is bound to a target wallet via an external input (extraData) so a relayer cannot redirect the registration.

externalInputs.name: walletAddress
externalInputs.description: 0x-prefixed, checksummed EVM address of the wallet being registered. Packed into one field element and exposed verbatim as public signal 5 (extraData). Binds the proof to the wallet: IdentityRegistry.register(proof, communityId, wallet) requires extraData == uint256(uint160(wallet)).

x-p2peace.note: Everything above follows registry.zk.email blueprint conventions and compiles as-is. Everything in this block is a project-specific circuit extension layered on the registry-generated core before trusted setup; it is NOT interpreted by the registry. See circuits/README.md section 3 (honesty box).
x-p2peace.domainInstancePolicy: One compiled instance per allowlisted government domain. The sender domain is constrained in-circuit by the fromDomain regex (all parts private: the domain is a compile-time constant, nothing needs revealing). The adapter contract exposes domainHash = keccak256('taxes.gov.example') as an immutable constant.

recipientCanonicalization.capture: recipientLocalBase (part index 1) plus the compile-time recipient-domain match
recipientCanonicalization.plusTagStripping: Structural, not computed: the capture group for the local part excludes '+', and the optional '+tag' segment is matched by a subsequent private part. The tag therefore never enters the nullifier preimage.
recipientCanonicalization.lowercasing: In-circuit per-byte gadget over the <=64-byte capture: for each byte b, if 65 <= b <= 90 then b += 32. ~6 constraints/byte; project-specific circom, applied before hashing.

nullifier.packing: Canonical recipient bytes packed 31 bytes per field element (up to 4 limbs for a 124-byte budget), then Poseidon over [limbs..., REGISTRATION_SALT].
nullifier.REGISTRATION_SALT: 0x70325032505f434954495a454e5f5245475f5631 (field element constant, ascii 'p2P2P_CITIZEN_REG_V1' packed; fixed protocol-wide so the nullifier is constant per email address across wallets and renewals)

emailTimestamp.primary: dkimTimestamp capture (DKIM t= tag): digits converted to an integer in-circuit; numeric, signed by the sending server. Set by Gmail/Google Workspace and most large senders.
emailTimestamp.fallback: If the sending domain omits t=, the instance is compiled with a Date:-header regex plus a date-to-unix gadget (as in zk-email's ether-email-auth) instead. Exactly one source is compiled in per instance; the signal meaning is identical.

publicSignals.name: domainHash
publicSignals.source: adapter constant keccak256(senderDomain); no raw signal

publicSignals.name: patternHash
publicSignals.source: adapter constant keccak256('p2peace/citizenship-v1@1'); no raw signal; binding is via the verifying key registered under this hash

x-p2peace.privacy: clientSideOnly=true: citizenship emails contain the prover's identity; proofs MUST be generated locally (SDK isLocal), never via the hosted remote prover.
x-p2peace.consumedBy: IdentityRegistry.register(EmailProof proof, uint8 communityId, address wallet); registry checks domainHash is allowlisted for communityId, nullifier unused (or rotating per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4), emailTimestamp >= now - maxProofAge (90d default).
